## WARDEN SOP Wardens have three main priorities to oversee within the Security Department: prisoner management, criminal processing, and armory and inventory management. The Warden is expected to focus on these priorities as the situation demands, but should not abandon any of these priorities unless there is an ongoing emergency. If there is no Head of Security, the Warden is also expected to lead and coordinate the Security department.
### Prisoner Management Wardens must ensure the security and safety of prisoners in the brig, and should attempt to fulfill any reasonable requests made by those prisoners. If the brig is not secure, the warden should move to resecure the brig immediately. The warden has the final say if visitations or deliveries are to be allowed into the brig. The warden is allowed to request another member of Security to assist them in fulfilling requests, especially if the request involves leaving the Security department.
When the crew transfer or evacuation shuttles have docked with the station, the Warden must ensure that all prisoners (regardless of sentence time) are brought to the security section of the shuttle for transportation to Central Command. Upon arrival at Central Command, prisoners are to be transferred in a timely manner to Midway holding cells.
### Criminal Processing The Warden is encouraged to handle the sentencing of any criminals caught during a shift, including relocating them to the proper brig or cell, allotting the appropriate time for their sentence, and releasing the prisoner when their sentence is complete. Wardens are strongly encouraged to consult with the arresting officer for the list of crimes that have been committed.
### Armory Management The warden is in charge of the station’s armory, and should not allow normal security personnel into the armory under normal conditions. It is recommended for the warden to document the list of all weapons and armor within the armory, and to distribute appropriate arms and munitions to other personnel as required by the current situation or any reasonable requests. The warden must be prompt in opening the armory to arm security during crisis, and equally prompt to ensure proper de-armament when crisis has passed.
## Security Mentor SOP Security mentors must always prioritize training and guiding other members of the security department, including (but not limited to) security cadets. Mentors are encouraged to take initiative with these teaching tasks, and must never avoid educating and guiding other members of the Security department when called upon. If no members of Security currently require training, security mentors are encouraged to assist the warden and Head of Security with their duties where reasonable.
## Detective SOP
### The Investigator
Detectives are discouraged from attempting to arrest suspects for crimes, unless ordered by the Head of Security or Captain, or if Security is experiencing a significant shortage of staff. If a Detective has encountered a crime in progress, they should call for assistance on Security comms before attempting an Arrest as per Method of Escalation (Ordinary arrests).
On alert levels higher than green, the detective is strongly encouraged to have their specialized forensic equipment on them.
If Detectives discover important and useful information regarding criminal investigations, they should notify Security personnel with the criminal records computer by marking individuals as Suspicious or Wanted. Evidence discovered should be mentioned in the criminal records Computer and over Telecomms.
Personnel should be marked as SUSPICIOUS if there are two or fewer pieces of evidence that strongly point to their involvement in a crime.
Personnel should be marked as WANTED if three or more pieces of evidence can strongly link them to their involvement in a crime or if there is already probable cause.
### Evidence Detectives should seek to collect and process as much evidence as possible when investigating crimes.
Common forms of evidence can include, but are not limited to: - DNA/Fingerprints on any items that have been displaced, used, or tampered with, including lockers and bags. - DNA or Fingerprints on nearby machinery and computers, such as Disposals Units. - DNA or Fingerprints on items a victim may have used to defend themselves during a violent crime. - DNA found within body fluids such as blood near the investigation area. - Airlock access logs (“Door logs”) for nearby airlocks, especially if recorded at a close time to when a crime was reported. - Witness reports of personnel within an area near the crime. These reports do not have to be worthy of Probable Cause. - Information from Medical personnel regarding the condition of the body (damage types, rotting state, etc.) if the crime may have been violent.
## Corpsman SOP
### Security and Medical Cooperation The corpsman is allowed access to the security and medical departments, including the tools, weapons, encrypted telecommunications channels, and chemicals found within. The Corpsman is also considered to be a member of the Security and Medical departments at the same time. The Corpsman must follow both security SOP and Medical SOP whenever possible, and should listen to orders from the Chief Medical Officer in addition to orders from the Head of Security and Captain/Acting Commanding Officer. The Corpsman is still required to perform the same duties as any Security Officer; including handling searches and arrests, and responding to calls for the security department. The Corpsman should not abandon Security duties for Medical duties, except when providing Emergency Aid to Security and Command personnel.
The Chief Medical Officer has the right to remove Medical access, and Medical access only, from the Corpsman as per normal Job Termination/Firing SOP. Corpsmen that are prioritizing Security SOP and orders from the Head of Security are not considered as "abandoning duty” for this purpose. The Head of Security, Head of Personnel, and Captain/ACO must be notified of this change by the CMO. In the event of a conflict of orders or interests, Security SOP and orders from the HoS or Captain has priority over Medical SOP and orders from the CMO.
The Corpsman may provide Emergency Aid (as defined in Medical SOP) to any personnel within their immediate area that require it. The Corpsman should not “chase” for wounded/critical/dead personnel outside of their immediate area unless those personnel are part of the Security or Command departments, if they are prisoners in the Brig or Permanent Confinement Area, or if given permission by the CMO or Captain. Corpsmen should bring or direct wounded personnel to Medical for Full Treatment whenever it is possible.
The Corpsman may provide Full Treatment (as defined in Medical SOP) to members of Command, Security, and prisoners, as long as they are within the Security department. The Corpsman may also provide Full Treatment to any personnel within the Medical department if given permission from the Captain or CMO, or if the Medbay is in a State of Crisis.
## Security Technician SOP
### Silicon Assistance and Breaching Duties Security Technicians are breaching and explosive handling specialists, intended to provide other Security members physical access to areas. Security Technicians are also provided with the necessary tools and materials to ensure that security-associated Silicon entities can be properly maintained. The Security Technician is still required to perform the same duties as any Security Officer; including handling searches and arrests, and responding to calls for the security department. The Security Technician is not authorized to construct, maintain, or service non-Security, non-personnel silicon entities unless granted permission by the Captain, Acting Commanding Officer, Station AI, or Mystagogue.
The Security Technician should be the only handler of demolition and breaching tools, such as the Breaching Hammer, Breaching Charges, Jaws of Life, and Detonation Cord. The carrying and utilization of these tools should be considered the same as non-sidearm lethal weaponry for the purposes of Alert Levels and Armory Procedure, with the exception of the Jaws of Life which may be carried on any Alert Level. Other personnel within the Security Department should not be handling these tools unless they are given authorization by the Warden or Head of Security. Security Technicians are provided with tools and insulated gloves for their work, but are not part of the Engineering department, and are not authorized to perform Engineering tasks at any time.
Servicing silicon entities will include the creation and installation/uninstallation of modules. The Service Technician will be held responsible for ensuring that Security Silicon non-personnel entities are properly equipped according to the current situation, including the station alert level. Non-personnel Silicon entities that are part of the Security Department must follow the orders of the Security Technician whenever possible.
Security Technicians may provide Emergency Aid (as defined in Medical SOP) to silicon personnel and entities within their immediate area that require it. They should not “chase” for damaged or incapacitated silicon entities outside of their immediate area unless those entities are associated with the Security or Command departments, if they are currently located within the Security or Command departments, or if given permission by the Mystagogue or Captain/ACO.
The Security Technician may provide Full Treatment (as defined in Medical SOP) to any silicon entities within the Security department, including the brig and permanent confinement area. Security Technicians should bring or direct damaged silicons to the Robotics lab for Full Treatment whenever it is possible.
The Security Technician is the most properly equipped person in Security for the handling and disposal of explosive devices, improvised or otherwise. Priority should be given to the Security Technician to handle, disable, and dispose of any unauthorized explosive devices on the station. The Security Technician should be wearing the Araa Tacsuit or a Bomb Disposal Suit when handling, defusing, and disposing of any unauthorized explosives, regardless of station alert level.
Proper disposal of unauthorized explosives should be done via controlled detonations away from the station whenever possible. It is strongly ill-advised to store unauthorized explosives inside of the station due to the potential for later detonation.
